name: Aesthefill
lead: AestheFill is an injectable poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) microsphere product made by REGEN Biotech of Seoul, South Korea. It contains PDLLA microspheres with carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) as a suspending agent, supplied as a lyophilised powder that is reconstituted with sterile water before injection, and is described as biocompatible, biodegradable and biostimulatory.[1][3][4]

It is used to correct soft-tissue volume loss in the face and, increasingly, the body. A randomised evaluator-blinded multicentre study compared it with hyaluronic acid for nasolabial fold augmentation.[1] Much of the other literature concerns reconstitution methods and consensus technique recommendations.[3][4][5][7]

paras: A randomised, evaluator-blinded, multicentre study published in Aesthetic Surgery Journal in 2024 compared injectable PDLLA (AestheFill) with hyaluronic acid for nasolabial fold augmentation, noting that its efficacy and safety had not previously been studied in a large cohort.[1]

A paper on non-surgical lower eyelid rejuvenation in Asian patients proposed a simple injection method using PDLLA.[2] Brazilian experts produced consensus recommendations using a modified Delphi method on reconstitution and use for facial and non-facial treatments.[3]

Several papers examine how the powder is prepared, since CMC can form lumps when mixed with water: studies discuss hydration and dispersion across six reconstitution methods, differences from the reconstitution of Sculptra, and a warm water soaking method to reduce micro-aggregates.[4][5][7] A separate paper describes the AestheCode guide for injection planning, and others describe the AestheBody guide for use beyond the face.[6][9][10] A 2025 physicochemical comparison characterised polylactic acid-based dermal fillers.[8]

card.summary: A Korean PDLLA microsphere biostimulator with one randomised trial against hyaluronic acid and a large body of technique papers.
card.note: Clinician-prepared product; much literature concerns reconstitution technique.

quick.overview:
AestheFill is a PDLLA microsphere injectable from REGEN Biotech used by clinicians to restore facial volume and, increasingly, body contour.

A randomised, evaluator-blinded multicentre trial compared it with hyaluronic acid for nasolabial folds, and expert consensus papers address its preparation.
quick.mechanism: PDLLA microspheres in carboxymethyl cellulose are reconstituted and injected; the product is described as biostimulatory, prompting tissue to restore volume over time.
quick.risks: Technique-related issues such as lumping during reconstitution are discussed in the literature. Specific adverse event rates were not summarised in the sources reviewed. It is administered by trained clinicians.
